# 3 Maccabees Chapter 2 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Alexandrinus) | **Section:** Ptolemy Struck Down and Then Persecutes

---

**1** Before he had even finished the prayer, the high priest Shimon, filled with awe and trembling, turned to Ptolemy and said: O Ptolemy, this great God who looks down from on high and watches over all things did not make this place holy for the sake of the wicked or for those who seek to force their way in against the law.

**2** He struck down the earlier Heliodorus, who came with a whole army to plunder the treasury, and drove him away in disgrace.

**3** And now, seeing you as someone who has transgressed against his laws, he will not leave you without punishment.

**4** He had barely finished these words when Ptolemy was seized with a tremendous terror. Every limb of his body was struck, and all strength drained out of him.

**5** His companions saw him collapse, and they rushed to carry him out, gripped themselves by fear.

**6** Thus God exercised his judgment, and Ptolemy was no longer capable of carrying out any of his threats.

**7** He returned to Egypt, bitter and humiliated, but God had delivered the people from harm.

**8** But back in Egypt, Ptolemy's wickedness grew worse and worse. Surrounded by worthless drinking companions who had no sense of justice, he was not satisfied with what he had already done.

**9** He began making threats against the Jews, and had a letter drafted commanding his soldiers to arrest all the Jews and imprison them wherever any of them might be found.

**10** When the letter was dispatched, it read: King Ptolemy Philopator to the generals and soldiers in Egypt and all its territories, greetings.

**11** I am well, and my affairs are in order.

**12** Since our campaign into Asia has gone as we intended and we have returned safely, we have decided, not through force but through goodwill and great generosity, to bestow benefits on the inhabitants of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.

**13** The Jews in those regions gave us a warm welcome and escorted us enthusiastically, and they accompanied us on our way and showed themselves helpful to us in every respect.

**14** However, many of these same Jews turn out to be troublemakers who refuse to submit to our authority, and they show contempt for our sacred shrines.

**15** Therefore, driven by kindness rather than anger, we have decided they should be registered in our population.

**16** They are to be enrolled in a census, assigned to the service class of our household, and all those registered are to be branded with the ivy-leaf emblem of Dionysus and reduced to the subordinate status they previously held.

**17** Those who refuse to accept this reduced status are to be arrested and punished; those who resist with contempt are to be executed.

**18** Our goal in all of this is to bring them to equal standing with us and to make them abandon their foreign and barbaric customs.

**19** Anyone who betrays a Jew or hands one over will receive the traitor's confiscated property as a reward.

**20** When this decree was read throughout Egypt, it caused great sorrow everywhere.

**21** The Jews were plunged into deep mourning and weeping, their hearts full of bitter anguish.

**22** Everywhere there were lamentations, weeping and grief filled the streets.

**23** People of gentle heart wept even for those who were in a lower situation than themselves.

**24** Grief settled over every household, and sighing and lamentation did not cease.

**25** The sorrow spread across all of Egypt, and no one was unmoved by the plight of the Jews.
